title: DSA offers and Secondary 1 places for non-affiliated students
asked: Ms Gho Sze Kee asked whether Direct School Admission offers reduce the Secondary 1 quota for students from non-affiliated schools, and whether any secondary school had no remaining slots for non-affiliated students after DSA and affiliation admissions.
response: MOE has required affiliated secondary schools to reserve at least 20% of Secondary 1 places for non-affiliated students since 2019, applied to each posting group. DSA admissions do not reduce a school's total Secondary 1 places, but non-affiliated students admitted through DSA count against the reserved places for non-affiliated students. Over the past five years, non-affiliated students made up about half of affiliated schools' Secondary 1 cohorts, and there were two instances where DSA filled all reserved places in one posting group, leaving no non-affiliated students posted in that group; other posting groups still admitted non-affiliated students.

key_points.point: Affiliated secondary schools must reserve at least 20% of Secondary 1 places for non-affiliated students.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: has required affiliated secondary schools to reserve at least 20% of places of their Secondary 1 cohort for non-affiliated students.

key_points.point: The 20% reservation is applied to each posting group.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: This requirement is applied to each posting group

key_points.point: Over the past five years, non-affiliated students made up about half of affiliated secondary schools' Secondary 1 cohorts.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: non-affiliated students have comprised about half of the Secondary 1 cohort of affiliated secondary schools.

key_points.point: A school's total Secondary 1 places are the sum of planned places under the Secondary 1 Posting Exercise and the DSA exercise.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The total number of Secondary 1 places offered in each school is the sum of planned places offered under the Secondary 1 Posting Exercise and the Direct School Admission (DSA) exercise.

key_points.point: DSA does not reduce a school's total Secondary 1 places, but non-affiliated DSA students take up reserved places for non-affiliated students.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: While the DSA admissions does not reduce the number of Secondary 1 places available in a school, non-affiliated students admitted via the DSA exercise will be considered as taking up reserved places for non-affiliated students.

key_points.point: In the past five years, there were two instances where DSA filled all reserved non-affiliated places in one posting group, and no non-affiliated students were posted in that group.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: In the past five years, there have been only two instances where an affiliated secondary school filled all the reserved places for non-affiliated students in one posting group via DSA, and no non-affiliated students were posted for that posting group during the Secondary 1 Posting Exercise.

key_points.point: In those cases, non-affiliated students in the other two posting groups were still admitted via the Secondary 1 Posting Exercise.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: However, non-affiliated students in the other two posting groups were still admitted via the Secondary 1 Posting Exercise.

left_open: The role of affiliation admissions, separately from DSA, in filling places for non-affiliated students.
supplementary: Supplementary questions asked about publishing DSA and affiliation admissions data, and about guidelines on affiliation score differentials.
